17: # Claude Code CLI - Complete Command Reference
18: 
19: Open this at dispatch time, when the command has to be right the first time: the tables answer what a switch does and what a failed run means.
20: 
21: ---
22: 
23: ## 1. OVERVIEW
24: 
25: ### Purpose
26: 
27: Provide a comprehensive, single-source reference for all Claude Code CLI commands, flags, models, configuration options, permission modes, and troubleshooting guidance for external AI assistants delegating tasks.
28: 
29: ### When to Use
30: 
31: - Setting up or configuring Claude Code CLI
32: - Looking up command-line flags, subcommands, or agent configurations
33: - Troubleshooting authentication, permission, or session issues
34: - Selecting the right model and permission mode for a task
35: - Understanding output formats and structured output options
36: 
37: ### Core Principle
38: 
39: Claude Code is Anthropic's official CLI for Claude, providing terminal-based AI coding assistance powered by Claude models (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku). It offers deep reasoning via extended thinking, surgical code editing, schema-validated structured output, agent delegation, and persistent memory — all from the command line.
40: 
41: ### Key Sources
42: 
43: | Source | URL |
44: |--------|-----|
45: | **Repository** | [anthropics/claude-code](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code) |
46: | **Documentation** | [Claude Code documentation](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code) |
47: | **License** | Proprietary (Anthropic) |
48: | **Runtime** | Node.js 18+ |
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## 2. INSTALLATION
53: 
54: | Method | Command | Notes |
55: |--------|---------|-------|
56: | **npm global** | `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` | Persistent install, recommended |
57: | **Upgrade** | `npm update -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` or `claude update` | Update to latest version |
58: 
59: **Platform support:**
60: 
61: | Platform | Status |
62: |----------|--------|
63: | macOS | Full support |
64: | Linux | Full support |
65: | Windows | Experimental |
66: 
67: After installation, run `claude` for interactive mode or `claude -p "prompt"` for non-interactive use.
68: 
69: ---
70: 
71: ## 3. AUTHENTICATION
72: 
73: cli-claude-code authenticates through the **Claude subscription OAuth only**. It does not use an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
74: 
75: | Method | Setup | Best For |
76: |--------|-------|----------|
77: | **OAuth** | `claude auth login` (browser flow) | Personal use, interactive |
78: | **Token Setup** | `claude setup-token` | Non-interactive CI/CD pipelines (long-lived OAuth token) |
79: 
80: **OAuth login/logout:**
81: 
82: ```bash
83: # Authenticate via browser (opens OAuth flow)
84: claude auth login
85: 
86: # View authentication status
87: claude auth status
88: 
89: # Log out
90: claude auth logout
91: ```
92: 
93: **Non-interactive token setup (CI/CD):**
94: 
95: ```bash
96: # Generate a long-lived OAuth token for headless environments
97: claude setup-token
98: ```
99: 
100: ---
101: 
102: ## 4. CORE INVOCATION
103: 
104: ### Non-Interactive Mode (Primary for Cross-AI)
105: 
106: The `-p` / `--print` flag is the primary invocation method for external AI delegation:
107: 
108: ```bash
109: claude -p "prompt" --output-format text 2>&1
110: ```
111: 
112: **CRITICAL**: Always append `2>&1` to capture both stdout and stderr.
113: 
114: ### Interactive Mode
115: 
116: ```bash
117: # Full-screen TUI (not suitable for cross-AI delegation)
118: claude
119: 
120: # Interactive with initial prompt
121: claude "Start by reviewing the auth module"
122: ```
123: 
124: ### Key Differences
125: 
126: | Mode | Flag | Output | Use Case |
127: |------|------|--------|----------|
128: | Non-interactive | `-p "prompt"` | stdout only, then exits | Cross-AI delegation, scripts, CI/CD |
129: | Interactive | (none) | Full TUI | Direct human use |
130: 
131: ---
132: 
133: ## 5. FLAGS REFERENCE
134: 
135: ### Primary Flags
136: 
137: | Flag | Short | Purpose | Example |
138: |------|-------|---------|---------|
139: | `--print` | `-p` | Non-interactive mode | `claude -p "Review this code"` |
140: | `--model` | | Model selection | `--model claude-sonnet-5-5` |
141: | `--output-format` | | Output format | `--output-format text` |
142: | `--permission-mode` | | Permission level | `--permission-mode plan` |
143: | `--agent` | | Route to agent | `--agent review` |
144: | `--json-schema` | | Schema validation | `--json-schema '{"type":"object",...}'` |
145: | `--max-budget-usd` | | Cost cap | `--max-budget-usd 1.00` |
146: | `--effort` | | Thinking effort | `--effort high` |
147: 
148: ### Session Management Flags
149: 
150: | Flag | Purpose | Example |
151: |------|---------|---------|
152: | `--continue` | Continue most recent conversation | `claude -p "Now fix it" --continue` |
153: | `--resume [value]` | Resume the most recent session, or a specific session when a value is supplied | `claude -p "Continue" --resume abc123` |
154: | `--fork-session` | Fork the session selected by `--resume` | `claude --resume abc123 --fork-session` |
155: 
156: ### Output Format Flags
157: 
158: | Format | Flag | Description |
159: |--------|------|-------------|
160: | **Text** | `--output-format text` | Plain text (default for `-p`) |
161: | **JSON** | `--output-format json` | JSON with metadata: `{role, content, cost, duration}` |
162: | **Stream JSON** | `--output-format stream-json` | Newline-delimited JSON for real-time processing |
163: 
164: ### Permission Mode Flags
165: 
166: | Mode | Flag | Behavior |
167: |------|------|----------|
168: | **Default** | (no flag) | Prompts for approval on writes and commands |
169: | **Accept Edits** | `--permission-mode acceptEdits` | Auto-approves file edits, prompts for shell commands |
170: | **Plan** | `--permission-mode plan` | Read-only — no file writes, no shell commands |
171: | **Don't Ask** | `--permission-mode dontAsk` | Skips unapproved tools silently |
172: | **Bypass** | `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` | Auto-approves everything — **dangerous** |
173: 
174: ### Effort Level
175: 
176: | Level | Flag | Behavior |
177: |-------|------|----------|
178: | **Default** | (no flag) | The effort the child's settings give it, else the model's built-in default |
179: | **Low** | `--effort low` | Fastest, least detailed: classification, formatting, mechanical edits |
180: | **Medium** | `--effort medium` | Routine edits and short reviews |
181: | **High** | `--effort high` | Extended thinking for standard code generation, reviews and debugging |
182: | **Extra high** | `--effort xhigh` | Architecture, hard trade-offs, subtle root causes |
183: | **Max** | `--effort max` | The hardest problems, where cost is secondary; pair with `--max-budget-usd` |
184: 
185: Every model in the roster below takes all five levels. When to use each one → [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md) §4.
186: 
187: ### Other Flags
188: 
189: | Flag | Purpose |
190: |------|---------|
191: | `--verbose` | Show detailed processing information |
192: | `--max-turns N` | Limit conversation turns |
193: | `--system-prompt "..."` | Override system prompt |
194: | `--append-system-prompt "..."` | Append to system prompt |
195: | `--allowedTools "tool1,tool2"` | Restrict available tools |
196: | `--disallowedTools "tool1,tool2"` | Disable specific tools |
197: | `--add-dir /path` | Add directory to context |
198: 
199: ---
200: 
201: ## 6. MODELS
202: 
203: **Full model catalog with tiers, defaults, and `--effort` mapping → [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md).**
204: 
205: ### Available Models
206: 
207: | Model | ID | Strengths | Cost | Best For |
208: |-------|----|-----------|------|----------|
209: | **Sonnet 5.5** | `claude-sonnet-5-5` | Balanced; the **skill default** | Medium | General tasks, code generation, reviews |
210: | **Opus 5.5** | `claude-opus-5-5` | Deepest Opus reasoning; the deep-reasoning override, paired with `--effort high` | High | Architecture decisions, complex trade-offs, extended thinking |
211: | **Haiku 5.5** | `claude-haiku-5-5` | Fastest, most cost-effective | Lowest | Classification, formatting, simple queries, batch ops |
212: | **Fable 5.1** | `claude-fable-5-1` | The current Fable; the CLI's `best` alias | UNKNOWN | Work routed to the Fable family by name |
213: 
214: All four take `--effort low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` and `max`. Claude Code 2.1.293 has no Fable 5.5: it rejects `claude-fable-5-5`, and `--model fable` resolves to `claude-fable-5-1`.
215: 
216: ---
217: 
218: ## 7. SUBCOMMANDS
219: 
220: | Subcommand | Purpose | Example |
221: |------------|---------|---------|
222: | `claude agents` | List available agents | `claude agents list` |
223: | `claude auth` | Authentication management | `claude auth login` / `claude auth logout` |
224: | `claude mcp` | MCP server management | `claude mcp list` / `claude mcp serve` |
225: | `claude plugin` | Plugin management | `claude plugin list` |
226: | `claude setup-token` | Non-interactive auth setup | `echo "$KEY" \| claude setup-token` |
227: | `claude update` | Update CLI to latest version | `claude update` |
228: 
229: ---
230: 
231: ## 8. CONTEXT HIERARCHY (CLAUDE.md)
232: 
233: Claude Code automatically loads context from CLAUDE.md files in a hierarchy:
234: 
235: | Level | Path | Scope |
236: |-------|------|-------|
237: | **Global** | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` | All projects for this user |
238: | **Project** | `PROJECT_ROOT/CLAUDE.md` | Current project |
239: | **Local** | `SUBDIR/CLAUDE.md` | Current directory (additive) |
240: 
241: **Context loading**: All three levels are merged. Project and local instructions override global where they conflict. Local instructions are additive.
242: 
243: **File references**: Use `@./path/to/file` in prompts to include file contents:
244: 
245: ```bash
246: claude -p "Review @./src/auth.ts and @./src/middleware.ts for security issues" \
247:   --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
248: ```
249: 
250: ---
251: 
252: ## 9. STRUCTURED OUTPUT
253: 
254: ### JSON Schema Validation
255: 
256: Claude Code can produce schema-validated JSON output using `--json-schema`:
257: 
258: ```bash
259: claude -p "Analyze src/utils.ts" \
260:   --json-schema '{"type":"object","properties":{"functions":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"params":{"type":"string"},"returnType":{"type":"string"},"complexity":{"type":"string"}}}},"issues":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"line":{"type":"number"},"severity":{"type":"string"},"description":{"type":"string"}}}}}}' \
261:   --output-format json 2>&1
262: ```
263: 
264: ### Output Format Comparison
265: 
266: | Format | Use When | Parsing |
267: |--------|----------|---------|
268: | `text` | Human consumption, simple integration | Direct string |
269: | `json` | Programmatic processing with metadata | `jq` or JSON parser |
270: | `json` + `--json-schema` | Guaranteed structure for pipelines | Schema-validated parse |
271: | `stream-json` | Real-time processing, progress tracking | Line-by-line JSON |
272: 
273: ### Parsing JSON Output
274: 
275: ```bash
276: # Extract content from JSON output
277: claude -p "List functions in src/utils.ts" --output-format json 2>&1 | jq -r '.result'
278: 
279: # With schema validation
280: claude -p "..." --json-schema '{"type":"object",...}' --output-format json 2>&1 | jq '.result'
281: ```
282: 
283: ---
284: 
285: ## 10. SESSION MANAGEMENT
286: 
287: ### Continue Last Session
288: 
289: ```bash
290: # Continue the most recent conversation
291: claude -p "Now apply the suggested fixes" --continue --output-format text 2>&1
292: ```
293: 
294: ### Resume Specific Session
295: 
296: ```bash
297: # Resume by session ID
298: claude -p "Continue where we left off" --resume SESSION_ID --output-format text 2>&1
299: ```
300: 
301: ### Fork Session
302: 
303: ```bash
304: # Fork from an existing session to try a different approach
305: claude --fork-session SESSION_ID -p "Try a different approach" --output-format text 2>&1
306: ```
307: 
308: ### Session IDs
309: 
310: Session IDs appear in JSON output format:
311: 
312: ```bash
313: # Get session ID from JSON output
314: claude -p "Start analyzing the auth module" --output-format json 2>&1 | jq -r '.session_id'
315: ```
316: 
317: ---
318: 
319: ## 11. ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
320: 
321: | Variable | Purpose |
322: |----------|---------|
323: | `CLAUDECODE` | Set when running inside Claude Code (nesting detection) |
324: | `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` | Disable telemetry |
325: | `CLAUDE_MODEL` | Default model override |
326: 
327: ### Nesting Detection
328: 
329: **CRITICAL**: The `CLAUDECODE` environment variable is automatically set when running inside a Claude Code session. External AIs must check this before invoking:
330: 
331: ```bash
332: # Check for nesting — abort if already inside Claude Code
333: if [ -n "$CLAUDECODE" ]; then
334:     echo "ERROR: Cannot invoke Claude Code from within a Claude Code session"
335:     exit 1
336: fi
337: ```
338: 
339: ---
340: 
341: ## 12. TROUBLESHOOTING
342: 
343: | Issue | Diagnosis | Solution |
344: |-------|-----------|----------|
345: | `claude: command not found` | Not installed | `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` |
346: | `401 Unauthorized` / not authenticated | Claude subscription OAuth not configured | Run `claude auth login` (or `claude setup-token` for CI/CD) |
347: | `Already inside Claude Code` | Nesting detected | Exit current session or use different terminal |
348: | Rate limit (429) | Too many requests | Wait for retry-after header; reduce frequency |
349: | Budget exceeded | `--max-budget-usd` cap hit | Increase budget or simplify prompt |
350: | Permission denied | Wrong permission mode | Use `--permission-mode plan` for read-only |
351: | Schema validation failed | JSON schema mismatch | Verify schema matches expected output structure |
352: | Context too large | Prompt + files exceed limit | Use `@` to reference specific files, not directories |
353: | Agent not found | Invalid agent name | Run `claude agents list` to see available agents |
354: | Session not found | Invalid resume ID | Check session ID from previous JSON output |
355: | Timeout | Long-running task | Use `--max-turns` to limit or run in background |
356: 
357: ### Common Patterns
358: 
359: ```bash
360: # Verbose mode for debugging
361: claude -p "..." --verbose --output-format text 2>&1
362: 
363: # Restrict tools for safety
364: claude -p "..." --allowedTools "Read,Glob,Grep" --output-format text 2>&1
365: 
366: # Cost-controlled execution
367: claude -p "..." --max-budget-usd 0.25 --output-format text 2>&1
368: ```
369: 
370: ---
371: 
372: ## 13. QUICK REFERENCE CARD
373: 
374: ```bash
375: # === ESSENTIAL PATTERNS ===
376: 
377: # Non-interactive (primary for cross-AI)
378: claude -p "prompt" --output-format text 2>&1
379: 
380: # Model selection
381: claude -p "prompt" --model claude-opus-5-5 --output-format text 2>&1
382: claude -p "prompt" --model claude-sonnet-5-5 --output-format text 2>&1
383: claude -p "prompt" --model claude-haiku-5-5 --output-format text 2>&1
384: claude -p "prompt" --model claude-fable-5-1 --output-format text 2>&1
385: 
386: # Effort (every roster model takes all five levels)
387: claude -p "prompt" --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort xhigh --output-format text 2>&1
388: 
389: # Permission modes
390: claude -p "prompt" --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1          # read-only
391: claude -p "prompt" --permission-mode acceptEdits --output-format text 2>&1   # auto-approve edits
392: 
393: # Structured output
394: claude -p "prompt" --json-schema '{"type":"object",...}' --output-format json 2>&1
395: 
396: # Agent delegation
397: claude -p "prompt" --agent review --output-format text 2>&1
398: 
399: # Session management
400: claude -p "prompt" --continue --output-format text 2>&1
401: claude -p "prompt" --resume SESSION_ID --output-format text 2>&1
402: 
403: # Cost control
404: claude -p "prompt" --max-budget-usd 1.00 --output-format text 2>&1
405: 
406: # Background execution
407: claude -p "prompt" --output-format text 2>&1 &
408: ```

175: 
176: | Level | Flag | Behavior |
177: |-------|------|----------|
178: | **Default** | (no flag) | The effort the child's settings give it, else the model's built-in default |
179: | **Low** | `--effort low` | Fastest, least detailed: classification, formatting, mechanical edits |
180: | **Medium** | `--effort medium` | Routine edits and short reviews |
181: | **High** | `--effort high` | Extended thinking for standard code generation, reviews and debugging |
182: | **Extra high** | `--effort xhigh` | Architecture, hard trade-offs, subtle root causes |
183: | **Max** | `--effort max` | The hardest problems, where cost is secondary; pair with `--max-budget-usd` |
184: 
185: Every model in the roster below takes all five levels. When to use each one → [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md) §4.
186: 
187: ### Other Flags
188: 
189: | Flag | Purpose |
190: |------|---------|
191: | `--verbose` | Show detailed processing information |
192: | `--max-turns N` | Limit conversation turns |
193: | `--system-prompt "..."` | Override system prompt |
194: | `--append-system-prompt "..."` | Append to system prompt |
195: | `--allowedTools "tool1,tool2"` | Restrict available tools |
196: | `--disallowedTools "tool1,tool2"` | Disable specific tools |
197: | `--add-dir /path` | Add directory to context |
198: 
199: ---
200: 
201: ## 6. MODELS
202: 
203: **Full model catalog with tiers, defaults, and `--effort` mapping → [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md).**
204: 
205: ### Available Models
206: 
207: | Model | ID | Strengths | Cost | Best For |
208: |-------|----|-----------|------|----------|
209: | **Sonnet 5.5** | `claude-sonnet-5-5` | Balanced; the **skill default** | Medium | General tasks, code generation, reviews |
210: | **Opus 5.5** | `claude-opus-5-5` | Deepest Opus reasoning; the deep-reasoning override, paired with `--effort high` | High | Architecture decisions, complex trade-offs, extended thinking |
211: | **Haiku 5.5** | `claude-haiku-5-5` | Fastest, most cost-effective | Lowest | Classification, formatting, simple queries, batch ops |
212: | **Fable 5.1** | `claude-fable-5-1` | The current Fable; the CLI's `best` alias | UNKNOWN | Work routed to the Fable family by name |
213: 
214: All four take `--effort low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` and `max`. Claude Code 2.1.293 has no Fable 5.5: it rejects `claude-fable-5-5`, and `--model fable` resolves to `claude-fable-5-1`.
215: 
216: ---
217: 
218: ## 7. SUBCOMMANDS
219: 
220: | Subcommand | Purpose | Example |
221: |------------|---------|---------|
222: | `claude agents` | List available agents | `claude agents list` |
223: | `claude auth` | Authentication management | `claude auth login` / `claude auth logout` |
224: | `claude mcp` | MCP server management | `claude mcp list` / `claude mcp serve` |
225: | `claude plugin` | Plugin management | `claude plugin list` |
226: | `claude setup-token` | Non-interactive auth setup | `echo "$KEY" \| claude setup-token` |
227: | `claude update` | Update CLI to latest version | `claude update` |
228: 
229: ---
230: 
231: ## 8. CONTEXT HIERARCHY (CLAUDE.md)
232: 
233: Claude Code automatically loads context from CLAUDE.md files in a hierarchy:
234: 
235: | Level | Path | Scope |
236: |-------|------|-------|
237: | **Global** | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` | All projects for this user |
238: | **Project** | `PROJECT_ROOT/CLAUDE.md` | Current project |
239: | **Local** | `SUBDIR/CLAUDE.md` | Current directory (additive) |
240: 
241: **Context loading**: All three levels are merged. Project and local instructions override global where they conflict. Local instructions are additive.
242: 
243: **File references**: Use `@./path/to/file` in prompts to include file contents:
244: 
245: ```bash
246: claude -p "Review @./src/auth.ts and @./src/middleware.ts for security issues" \
247:   --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
248: ```
249: 
250: ---
251: 
252: ## 9. STRUCTURED OUTPUT
253: 
254: ### JSON Schema Validation
255: 
256: Claude Code can produce schema-validated JSON output using `--json-schema`:
257: 
258: ```bash
259: claude -p "Analyze src/utils.ts" \
260:   --json-schema '{"type":"object","properties":{"functions":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"params":{"type":"string"},"returnType":{"type":"string"},"complexity":{"type":"string"}}}},"issues":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"line":{"type":"number"},"severity":{"type":"string"},"description":{"type":"string"}}}}}}' \
261:   --output-format json 2>&1
262: ```
263: 
264: ### Output Format Comparison
265: 
266: | Format | Use When | Parsing |
267: |--------|----------|---------|
268: | `text` | Human consumption, simple integration | Direct string |
269: | `json` | Programmatic processing with metadata | `jq` or JSON parser |
270: | `json` + `--json-schema` | Guaranteed structure for pipelines | Schema-validated parse |
271: | `stream-json` | Real-time processing, progress tracking | Line-by-line JSON |
272: 
273: ### Parsing JSON Output
274: 
275: ```bash
276: # Extract content from JSON output
277: claude -p "List functions in src/utils.ts" --output-format json 2>&1 | jq -r '.result'
278: 
279: # With schema validation
280: claude -p "..." --json-schema '{"type":"object",...}' --output-format json 2>&1 | jq '.result'
281: ```
282: 
283: ---
284: 
285: ## 10. SESSION MANAGEMENT
286: 
287: ### Continue Last Session
288: 
289: ```bash
290: # Continue the most recent conversation
291: claude -p "Now apply the suggested fixes" --continue --output-format text 2>&1
292: ```
293: 
294: ### Resume Specific Session
295: 
296: ```bash
297: # Resume by session ID
298: claude -p "Continue where we left off" --resume SESSION_ID --output-format text 2>&1
299: ```
300: 
301: ### Fork Session
302: 
303: ```bash
304: # Fork from an existing session to try a different approach
305: claude --fork-session SESSION_ID -p "Try a different approach" --output-format text 2>&1
306: ```
307: 
308: ### Session IDs
309: 
310: Session IDs appear in JSON output format:
311: 
312: ```bash
313: # Get session ID from JSON output
314: claude -p "Start analyzing the auth module" --output-format json 2>&1 | jq -r '.session_id'
315: ```
316: 
317: ---
318: 
319: ## 11. ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
320: 
321: | Variable | Purpose |
322: |----------|---------|
323: | `CLAUDECODE` | Set when running inside Claude Code (nesting detection) |
324: | `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` | Disable telemetry |
325: | `CLAUDE_MODEL` | Default model override |
326: 
327: ### Nesting Detection
328: 
329: **CRITICAL**: The `CLAUDECODE` environment variable is automatically set when running inside a Claude Code session. External AIs must check this before invoking:
330: 
331: ```bash
332: # Check for nesting — abort if already inside Claude Code
333: if [ -n "$CLAUDECODE" ]; then
334:     echo "ERROR: Cannot invoke Claude Code from within a Claude Code session"
335:     exit 1
336: fi
337: ```
338: 
339: ---
340: 
341: ## 12. TROUBLESHOOTING
342: 
343: | Issue | Diagnosis | Solution |
344: |-------|-----------|----------|
345: | `claude: command not found` | Not installed | `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` |
346: | `401 Unauthorized` / not authenticated | Claude subscription OAuth not configured | Run `claude auth login` (or `claude setup-token` for CI/CD) |
347: | `Already inside Claude Code` | Nesting detected | Exit current session or use different terminal |
348: | Rate limit (429) | Too many requests | Wait for retry-after header; reduce frequency |
349: | Budget exceeded | `--max-budget-usd` cap hit | Increase budget or simplify prompt |
350: | Permission denied | Wrong permission mode | Use `--permission-mode plan` for read-only |
351: | Schema validation failed | JSON schema mismatch | Verify schema matches expected output structure |
352: | Context too large | Prompt + files exceed limit | Use `@` to reference specific files, not directories |
353: | Agent not found | Invalid agent name | Run `claude agents list` to see available agents |
354: | Session not found | Invalid resume ID | Check session ID from previous JSON output |
355: | Timeout | Long-running task | Use `--max-turns` to limit or run in background |
356: 
357: ### Common Patterns
358: 
359: ```bash
360: # Verbose mode for debugging
361: claude -p "..." --verbose --output-format text 2>&1
362: 
363: # Restrict tools for safety
364: claude -p "..." --allowedTools "Read,Glob,Grep" --output-format text 2>&1
365: 
366: # Cost-controlled execution
367: claude -p "..." --max-budget-usd 0.25 --output-format text 2>&1
368: ```
369: 
370: ---
371: 
372: ## 13. QUICK REFERENCE CARD
373: 
374: ```bash
375: # === ESSENTIAL PATTERNS ===
376: 
377: # Non-interactive (primary for cross-AI)
378: claude -p "prompt" --output-format text 2>&1
379: 
380: # Model selection
381: claude -p "prompt" --model claude-opus-5-5 --output-format text 2>&1
382: claude -p "prompt" --model claude-sonnet-5-5 --output-format text 2>&1
383: claude -p "prompt" --model claude-haiku-5-5 --output-format text 2>&1
384: claude -p "prompt" --model claude-fable-5-1 --output-format text 2>&1
385: 
386: # Effort (every roster model takes all five levels)
387: claude -p "prompt" --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort xhigh --output-format text 2>&1
388: 
389: # Permission modes
390: claude -p "prompt" --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1          # read-only
391: claude -p "prompt" --permission-mode acceptEdits --output-format text 2>&1   # auto-approve edits
392: 
393: # Structured output
394: claude -p "prompt" --json-schema '{"type":"object",...}' --output-format json 2>&1
395: 
396: # Agent delegation
397: claude -p "prompt" --agent review --output-format text 2>&1
398: 
399: # Session management
400: claude -p "prompt" --continue --output-format text 2>&1
401: claude -p "prompt" --resume SESSION_ID --output-format text 2>&1
402: 
403: # Cost control
404: claude -p "prompt" --max-budget-usd 1.00 --output-format text 2>&1
405: 
406: # Background execution
407: claude -p "prompt" --output-format text 2>&1 &
408: ```

14: 
15: # cli-claude-code Providers, Models & Invocation
16: 
17: The single catalog of the provider, model ids, defaults, `--effort` thinking lever, and dispatch shapes the cli-claude-code mode can reach.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: ### Purpose
24: 
25: One place to answer "which model, which effort, how to dispatch" for cli-claude-code.
26: 
27: ### When to Use
28: - Choosing a `--model claude-*` id for a `claude -p` dispatch
29: - Mapping a desired reasoning depth onto the `--effort` flag
30: - Recalling the default model and the canonical non-interactive invocation shape
31: 
32: ### Core Principle
33: 
34: This mode is single-provider (Anthropic) and always reaches a small, fixed roster — so this file IS the catalog, with every model id inline.
35: 
36: ### Scope
37: This file enumerates the model/effort facts and the dispatch envelope. It does NOT own: the full `claude` flag surface, permission modes, auth pre-flight, and troubleshooting (see [cli-reference.md](./cli-reference.md)), per-model prompt-craft (see §6), or the fan-out / model-enforcement runtime (see §6).
38: 
39: ### Authority pointers
40: - Full CLI flags, subcommands, permission modes, OAuth pre-flight, troubleshooting → [cli-reference.md](./cli-reference.md)
41: - Dispatch shapes + orchestration patterns → [integration-patterns.md](./integration-patterns.md)
42: - Live model availability on a given install → the calling environment's `--model` support
43: 
44: ---
45: 
46: ## 2. PROVIDERS & MODELS
47: 
48: cli-claude-code is single-provider: **Anthropic**. The model string passed to `--model` is always a `claude-*` id. The roster below is complete. Pin the exact id; the CLI also accepts the aliases `opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku` and `fable`, which resolve to the newest id in each family.
49: 
50: ### Anthropic
51: 
52: | Model id | Default? | Role | Efforts |
53: |----------|----------|------|---------|
54: | `claude-sonnet-5-5` | **Default** | Sonnet 5.5, balanced: general tasks, code generation, reviews | all five |
55: | `claude-opus-5-5` | no | Opus 5.5, deepest Opus reasoning: architecture, complex trade-offs, subtle root causes | all five |
56: | `claude-haiku-5-5` | no | Haiku 5.5, fastest and cheapest: classification, formatting, simple queries, batch work. Use when the caller asks for it | all five |
57: | `claude-fable-5-1` | no | Fable 5.1, the current Fable. The CLI's model catalog names `fable` as its `best` alias | all five |
58: 
59: > **No Fable 5.5 yet.** Claude Code 2.1.293 rejects `claude-fable-5-5` with `unrecognized_model`, and its `fable` alias resolves to `claude-fable-5-1`. Pin `claude-fable-5-1`, or pass `--model fable` to get whichever Fable the installed CLI knows. Recheck with `claude -p --model claude-fable-5-5 --effort low "Reply with OK" </dev/null 2>&1` after a CLI update.
60: 
61: **Replaced ids.** The previous default `claude-sonnet-4-6` and the earlier `claude-sonnet-5` give way to `claude-sonnet-5-5`, and `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` gives way to `claude-haiku-5-5`. The old ids were not probed when this roster was refreshed, so pin one only after confirming it answers.
62: 
63: ---
64: 
65: ## 3. DEFAULTS & QUICK INVOCATION
66: 
67: Dispatch this mode's default without opening any other file:
68: 
69: | Field | Value |
70: |-------|-------|
71: | Default model | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
72: | Default effort | none passed; the child resolves it (see §4) |
73: | Default format | `--output-format text` |
74: 
75: ```bash
76: claude -p "<prompt>" \
77:   --model claude-sonnet-5-5 \
78:   --output-format text \
79:   2>&1
80: ```
81: 
82: - Always append `2>&1` to capture both stdout and stderr.
83: - For deep-reasoning work, override with `--model claude-opus-5-5 --effort high`, and raise the effort to `xhigh` or `max` when `high` is not enough.
84: - If Claude Code is not authenticated, the mode ASKS the operator to run `claude auth login`; it never substitutes an API key or a different model. See the OAuth pre-flight decision tree in [cli-reference.md](./cli-reference.md) §3 and the SKILL's "Provider Auth Pre-Flight".
85: 
86: **Why Sonnet 5.5 is the default.** It answered a live probe, it is what the `sonnet` alias resolves to, and it keeps the default in the same balanced family as before, so a caller that names no model gets the same cost and depth profile on the current generation. Opus and Fable stay opt-in for work that needs more depth.
87: 
88: ---
89: 
90: ## 4. REASONING-EFFORT / THINKING LEVER
91: 
92: cli-claude-code expresses reasoning depth through the **`--effort`** flag. Every model in §2 takes all five levels: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` and `max`. Claude Code 2.1.293 lists those five values in `claude --help`, and its model catalog marks each roster model with the `effort`, `xhigh_effort` and `max_effort` capabilities.
93: 
94: | Level | Flag | When to use it |
95: |-------|------|----------------|
96: | Low | `--effort low` | Classification, formatting, quick lookups, mechanical edits. Fastest and cheapest |
97: | Medium | `--effort medium` | Routine edits and short reviews. The built-in default of the 5.5 models |
98: | High | `--effort high` | Standard code generation, reviews and debugging. The usual pairing with Opus |
99: | Extra high | `--effort xhigh` | Architecture, hard trade-offs, subtle root causes, deep reviews |
100: | Max | `--effort max` | The hardest problems, where cost is secondary. Pair it with `--max-budget-usd` |
101: 
102: **When the flag is omitted.** The child takes the effort its loaded settings give it, a top-level `effortLevel` or a per-model entry under `modelSettings`, and otherwise the model's built-in default. Those settings set a model's default only. They never remove a level, so `--effort` always reaches all five. Pass `--effort` whenever the depth matters, so the result does not depend on the machine's settings.
103: 
104: ---
105: 
106: ## 5. HOW TO INVOKE
107: 
108: ### Self-invocation guard
109: A `claude -p` dispatch must never run from inside a Claude Code session (a `$CLAUDECODE`-set, `claude`-in-ancestry, or state-lock signal) — that is a circular self-invocation. The guard is inline in [../ROUTER.md](../ROUTER.md) §3 "Self-Invocation Guard".
110: 
111: ### Dispatch envelope (child / detached sessions)
112: When dispatching as a non-interactive child (spec-gate-neutralized worker), prefix the shared env and capture stderr:
113: 
114: ```bash
115: SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 claude -p "<prompt>" \
116:   --model claude-sonnet-5-5 --output-format text 2>&1
117: ```
118: 
119: - `SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` — neutralizes the spec-gate for a bound child worker so it does not stall on an interactive Gate-3 answer, and marks the run as an orchestrated sub-session so the worktree wrapper exec's in place rather than allocating its own worktree. See [../SKILL.md](../SKILL.md) §4 Rule 13.
120: - `2>&1` — REQUIRED to capture stderr; without it error and warning messages are lost. See [integration-patterns.md](./integration-patterns.md).
121: - `-p` (print) is mandatory for non-interactive dispatch; use `--permission-mode plan` for read-only review/analysis.
122: 
123: ### Parallel / fan-out
124: Multi-lineage parallel dispatch is driven by `fanout-run.cjs`, which lives outside this hub — see §6.
125: 
126: ---
127: 
128: ## 6. ENFORCEMENT & PROFILES (authoritative elsewhere — do not duplicate here)
129: 
130: - **Fan-out dispatcher + model enforcement** → [fanout-run.cjs](../../../system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs)
131: - **Live model availability** → the calling environment's `--model` support on the target install
132: 
133: ---
134: 
135: ## 7. RELATED
136: 
137: - [cli-reference.md](./cli-reference.md) — full `claude` flags, subcommands, permission modes, OAuth pre-flight, troubleshooting
138: - [integration-patterns.md](./integration-patterns.md) — cross-AI orchestration patterns and dispatch shapes
139: - [../SKILL.md](../SKILL.md) — cli-claude-code mode overview and default-invocation contract
140: - [../ROUTER.md](../ROUTER.md) — machine router: intent map, resource map, loading levels and the self-invocation guard

17:

19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Purpose
25: 
26: Each pattern documented here includes the rationale, implementation template, and practical considerations for combining an external AI with Claude Code CLI effectively.
27: 
28: ### When to Use
29: 
30: - You need Claude Code's deep reasoning or extended thinking for a specific subtask
31: - Schema-validated structured output is needed for pipeline integration
32: - Surgical code editing through Claude Code's Edit tool
33: - Cross-AI validation where a second perspective catches blind spots
34: - Cost-controlled execution with `--max-budget-usd`
35: - Read-only exploration with guaranteed safety via `--permission-mode plan`
36: 
37: ### Core Principle
38: 
39: The calling AI acts as the orchestrator (planner, validator, integrator) while Claude Code CLI executes targeted tasks. This is the **reverse** of the cli-opencode and cli-claude-code skills where Claude Code conducts. Here, Claude Code is the executor.
40: 
41: ---
42: 
43: ## 2. GENERATE-REVIEW-FIX CYCLE
44: 
45: **The most reliable cross-AI pattern.** The calling AI generates, Claude Code reviews, the calling AI fixes.
46: 
47: ### When to Use
48: 
49: - Code generation tasks where a second perspective catches edge cases
50: - Security-sensitive code where independent review adds confidence
51: - Architecture decisions that benefit from adversarial review
52: 
53: ### Flow
54: 
55: ```
56: Calling AI (generate) --> Claude Code (review) --> Calling AI (fix)
57: ```
58: 
59: ### Implementation
60: 
61: ```bash
62: # Step 1: Calling AI generates code, saves to /tmp/generated.ts
63: 
64: # Step 2: Claude Code reviews (read-only)
65: claude -p "Review @/tmp/generated.ts for bugs, security issues, and style violations. Be specific about line numbers and severity." \
66:   --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1 > /tmp/review.md
67: 
68: # Step 3: Calling AI reads review, applies fixes to /tmp/generated.ts
69: ```
70: 
71: ### Considerations
72: 
73: - Use `--permission-mode plan` for the review step (guaranteed read-only)
74: - Keep the review prompt focused: request specific findings, not general feedback
75: - Limit to 2 fix cycles maximum; diminishing returns beyond that
76: 
77: ---
78: 
79: ## 3. DEEP REASONING DELEGATION
80: 
81: **Leverage extended thinking for complex decisions.** Delegate tasks requiring multi-dimensional analysis to Claude Code's Opus model with extended thinking.
82: 
83: ### When to Use
84: 
85: - Architecture decisions with 4+ competing concerns
86: - Algorithm design requiring correctness analysis
87: - Root cause analysis where surface-level debugging failed
88: - Technical decisions that will be hard to reverse
89: 
90: ### Flow
91: 
92: ```
93: Calling AI (identify decision) --> Claude Code (deep analysis) --> Calling AI (implement decision)
94: ```
95: 
96: ### Implementation
97: 
98: ```bash
99: # Architecture decision
100: claude -p "We need to choose between event sourcing and CRUD for order management. Analyze trade-offs across: data consistency, query performance, team learning curve, operational complexity, and future scalability. Recommend with confidence level." \
101:   --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort high --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1 > /tmp/analysis.md
102: 
103: # Algorithm design
104: claude -p "Design a rate limiting algorithm that supports: per-user limits, sliding window, burst allowance, and distributed operation. Analyze time/space complexity for each approach." \
105:   --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort high --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1 > /tmp/algorithm.md
106: 
107: # Root cause analysis
108: claude -p "Intermittent 500 errors on POST /api/orders. Error logs show: [paste logs]. Analyze @src/api/orders.ts and @src/services/order.ts. Identify all possible root causes ranked by likelihood." \
109:   --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort high --agent debug --output-format text 2>&1 > /tmp/rca.md
110: ```
111: 
112: ### Considerations
113: 
114: - Use `claude-opus-5-5` with `--effort high`, and raise it to `xhigh` or `max` for maximum reasoning depth
115: - Use `--permission-mode plan` when analysis doesn't need file writes
116: - Opus is expensive — reserve for genuinely complex decisions
117: - Sonnet with `--effort high` is a good middle ground for moderately complex tasks
118: 
119: ---
120: 
121: ## 4. STRUCTURED OUTPUT PROCESSING
122: 
123: **Extract structured data from Claude Code for programmatic use.**
124: 
125: ### When to Use
126: 
127: - Pipeline integration requiring guaranteed JSON structure
128: - Batch analysis producing machine-readable results
129: - Data extraction that feeds into automated workflows
130: - Comparative analysis across multiple files
131: 
132: ### Implementation
133: 
134: ```bash
135: # Function analysis with schema validation
136: claude -p "Analyze all exported functions in @src/utils.ts" \
137:   --json-schema '{"type":"object","properties":{"functions":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"params":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"returnType":{"type":"string"},"complexity":{"type":"string","enum":["low","medium","high"]}},"required":["name","returnType"]}}}}' \
138:   --output-format json 2>&1 > /tmp/analysis.json
139: 
140: # Parse with jq
141: jq '.result.functions[] | select(.complexity == "high")' /tmp/analysis.json
142: 
143: # Security findings with structured severity
144: claude -p "Audit @src/auth/ for security vulnerabilities" \
145:   --json-schema '{"type":"object","properties":{"findings":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"severity":{"type":"string","enum":["critical","high","medium","low"]},"file":{"type":"string"},"line":{"type":"number"},"description":{"type":"string"},"fix":{"type":"string"}},"required":["severity","description"]}},"summary":{"type":"string"}}}' \
146:   --output-format json 2>&1 > /tmp/audit.json
147: ```
148: 
149: ### Considerations
150: 
151: - Always specify `--output-format json` alongside `--json-schema`
152: - Keep schemas focused — complex schemas increase failure probability
153: - Test schema with a small prompt before batch operations
154: - Parse with `jq '.result'` to extract the content from the JSON wrapper
155: 
156: ---
157: 
158: ## 5. BACKGROUND EXECUTION
159: 
160: **Run Claude Code tasks in parallel while the calling AI continues working.**
161: 
162: ### When to Use
163: 
164: - Long-running analysis or generation tasks
165: - Parallel processing of independent subtasks
166: - Documentation generation while working on code
167: 
168: ### Implementation
169: 
170: ```bash
171: # Start background task
172: claude -p "Generate comprehensive tests for @src/services/" \
173:   --max-budget-usd 0.50 --output-format text 2>&1 > /tmp/tests-output.txt &
174: CLAUDE_PID=$!
175: 
176: # Calling AI continues with other work...
177: 
178: # Check if done
179: if kill -0 $CLAUDE_PID 2>/dev/null; then
180:     echo "Still running..."
181: else
182:     echo "Done. Output in /tmp/tests-output.txt"
183: fi
184: 
185: # Wait for completion
186: wait $CLAUDE_PID
187: ```
188: 
189: ### Considerations
190: 
191: - Always use `--max-budget-usd` for background tasks to prevent runaway costs
192: - Redirect output to a file (`> /tmp/output.txt`) for later retrieval
193: - Use `$!` to capture the PID for status checking
194: - Background tasks compete for API rate limits
195: 
196: ---
197: 
198: ## 6. MODEL SELECTION STRATEGY
199: 
200: **Choose the right model tier for each delegated task.**
201: 
202: ### Decision Matrix
203: 
204: | Task Complexity | Model | Flag | Cost Tier |
205: |----------------|-------|------|-----------|
206: | Trivial (classify, format) | Haiku | `--model claude-haiku-5-5` | Low |
207: | Standard (review, generate) | Sonnet | `--model claude-sonnet-5-5` | Medium |
208: | Complex (architecture, debug) | Opus | `--model claude-opus-5-5 --effort high` | High |
209: 
210: ### Implementation
211: 
212: ```bash
213: # Tier 1: Haiku for fast, cheap tasks
214: claude -p "Classify these error messages by type: [errors]" \
215:   --model claude-haiku-5-5 --output-format text 2>&1
216: 
217: # Tier 2: Sonnet for standard tasks (default)
218: claude -p "Review @src/auth.ts for security issues" \
219:   --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
220: 
221: # Tier 3: Opus for complex reasoning
222: claude -p "Design the data migration strategy for moving from MongoDB to PostgreSQL" \
223:   --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort high --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
224: ```
225: 
226: ### Cost Optimization
227: 
228: ```bash
229: # Quick triage with Haiku, then deep dive with Opus on critical items
230: TRIAGE=$(claude -p "List the 3 most critical security issues in @src/auth/" \
231:   --model claude-haiku-5-5 --output-format text 2>&1)
232: 
233: DEEP_ANALYSIS=$(claude -p "Deep analysis of these security issues: $TRIAGE" \
234:   --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort high --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1)
235: ```
236: 
237: ---
238: 
239: ## 7. CONTEXT ENRICHMENT
240: 
241: **Provide rich context to Claude Code for better results.**
242: 
243: ### CLAUDE.md Context
244: 
245: Claude Code automatically loads CLAUDE.md files. Place project context there for consistent behavior:
246: 
247: ```
248: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md           → Global preferences
249: PROJECT_ROOT/CLAUDE.md        → Project conventions, architecture
250: SUBDIR/CLAUDE.md              → Module-specific context
251: ```
252: 
253: ### File References
254: 
255: Use `@` prefix to include file contents in prompts:
256: 
257: ```bash
258: # Single file
259: claude -p "Review @src/auth.ts" --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
260: 
261: # Multiple files
262: claude -p "Review @src/auth.ts and @src/middleware/auth.ts for consistency" \
263:   --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
264: 
265: # Combining context with task
266: claude -p "Given the patterns in @src/middleware/auth.ts, create similar middleware for rate limiting" \
267:   --output-format text 2>&1
268: ```
269: 
270: ### System Prompt Enhancement
271: 
272: ```bash
273: # Append context to system prompt
274: claude -p "Review this code" \
275:   --append-system-prompt "Project uses Express.js 4.x, TypeScript strict mode, and Jest for testing. Follow OWASP Top 10 guidelines." \
276:   --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
277: ```
278: 
279: ---
280: 
281: ## 8. VALIDATION PIPELINE
282: 
283: **Multi-stage validation using Claude Code at different levels.**
284: 
285: ### When to Use
286: 
287: - Pre-merge quality gates
288: - Complex feature development requiring multiple review dimensions
289: - Security-sensitive changes requiring independent validation
290: 
291: ### 5-Stage Pipeline
292: 
293: ```bash
294: # Stage 1: Syntax check (calling AI or local tools)
295: npx tsc --noEmit src/feature.ts
296: 
297: # Stage 2: Security review (Claude Code, read-only)
298: claude -p "Security audit of @src/feature.ts. Check OWASP Top 10." \
299:   --agent review --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1 > /tmp/security.md
300: 
301: # Stage 3: Architecture review (Claude Code, read-only)
302: claude -p "Does @src/feature.ts follow the patterns in @src/services/? Check coupling, error handling, typing." \
303:   --agent review --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1 > /tmp/arch.md
304: 
305: # Stage 4: Test coverage analysis (Claude Code, read-only)
306: claude -p "Analyze @src/feature.ts and suggest comprehensive test cases. Identify edge cases and error paths." \
307:   --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1 > /tmp/test-plan.md
308: 
309: # Stage 5: Final integration review (calling AI)
310: # Read all review outputs and make final decision
311: ```
312: 
313: ---
314: 
315: ## 9. CROSS-VALIDATION
316: 
317: **Use multiple AIs to validate the same artifact.**
318: 
319: ### When to Use
320: 
321: - High-stakes code changes (auth, payments, data handling)
322: - Architecture decisions that are hard to reverse
323: - Security audits where coverage matters more than speed
324: 
325: ### Implementation
326: 
327: ```bash
328: # Calling AI generates code, saves to /tmp/feature.ts
329: 
330: # Claude Code reviews
331: CLAUDE_REVIEW=$(claude -p "Review @/tmp/feature.ts for bugs and security issues" \
332:   --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1)
333: 
334: # OpenCode reviews (if available)
335: OPENCODE_REVIEW=$(opencode run "Review @/tmp/feature.ts for bugs and security issues" \
336:   --sandbox read-only --model gpt-5.3-opencode 2>&1)
337: 
338: # Calling AI synthesizes all reviews
339: # Compare findings, prioritize issues found by multiple AIs
340: ```
341: 
342: ### Considerations
343: 
344: - Cross-validation is expensive (3x cost) — reserve for critical code
345: - Focus on disagreements between AIs as areas needing human review
346: - Weight each AI's strengths: Claude for reasoning, OpenCode for sandbox safety and web context
347: 
348: ---
349: 
350: ## 10. SESSION CONTINUITY
351: 
352: **Continue conversations across invocations.**
353: 
354: ### When to Use
355: 
356: - Multi-step analysis where each step builds on the previous
357: - Iterative refinement of complex outputs
358: - Long-running investigations that span multiple invocations
359: 
360: ### Implementation
361: 
362: ```bash
363: # Initial analysis
364: claude -p "Analyze the auth module architecture" --output-format json 2>&1 > /tmp/session1.json
365: 
366: # Extract session info for resumption
367: SESSION_ID=$(jq -r '.session_id' /tmp/session1.json)
368: 
369: # Continue the conversation
370: claude -p "Now suggest improvements to the auth flow you identified" \
371:   --continue --output-format text 2>&1
372: 
373: # Or resume a specific session
374: claude -p "Apply the suggested improvements" \
375:   --resume "$SESSION_ID" --output-format text 2>&1
376: ```
377: 
378: ### Considerations
379: 
380: - `--continue` always continues the most recent session
381: - `--resume SESSION_ID` is more reliable for specific conversations
382: - Session context accumulates — watch for growing token usage and costs
383: - Use `--max-budget-usd` to cap cumulative session costs
384: 
385: ---
386: 
387: ## 11. ANTI-PATTERNS
388: 
389: ### Don't Do These
390: 
391: | Anti-Pattern | Problem | Better Approach |
392: |-------------|---------|-----------------|
393: | **Delegating trivial tasks** | CLI overhead > task cost | Handle simple tasks locally |
394: | **Skipping validation** | AI output can be wrong | Always validate before integrating |
395: | **Nesting Claude Code** | Undefined behavior when `$CLAUDECODE` is set | Check env var; use different terminal |
396: | **Ignoring costs** | Background tasks can accumulate | Always use `--max-budget-usd` |
397: | **Broad prompts** | "Review the whole project" overwhelms context | Target specific files with `@` |
398: | **Wrong model for task** | Opus for classification wastes money | Match model tier to complexity |
399: | **Skipping `2>&1`** | Lose error messages | Always capture stderr |
400: | **Trusting blindly** | Any AI can produce incorrect output | Cross-reference with codebase |
401: | **Rapid sequential calls** | Hit rate limits | Batch operations or add delays |
402: | **Using `bypassPermissions`** | Dangerous auto-approve | Always get explicit user approval |
403: 
404: ### Cost Awareness
405: 
406: ```
407: Approximate cost comparison (per 1K input + 1K output tokens):
408:   Haiku:  ~$0.001 (cheapest)
409:   Sonnet: ~$0.01  (10x haiku)
410:   Opus:   ~$0.05  (50x haiku)
411: 
412: Rule of thumb:
413:   - Haiku for batch/simple: $0.01-0.05 per task
414:   - Sonnet for standard: $0.05-0.25 per task
415:   - Opus for complex: $0.25-2.00 per task
416: 
417: Always use --max-budget-usd for batch operations.
418: ```

154: - Parse with `jq '.result'` to extract the content from the JSON wrapper
155: 
156: ---
157: 
158: ## 5. BACKGROUND EXECUTION
159: 
160: **Run Claude Code tasks in parallel while the calling AI continues working.**
161: 
162: ### When to Use
163: 
164: - Long-running analysis or generation tasks
165: - Parallel processing of independent subtasks
166: - Documentation generation while working on code
167: 
168: ### Implementation
169: 
170: ```bash
171: # Start background task
172: claude -p "Generate comprehensive tests for @src/services/" \
173:   --max-budget-usd 0.50 --output-format text 2>&1 > /tmp/tests-output.txt &
174: CLAUDE_PID=$!
175: 
176: # Calling AI continues with other work...
177: 
178: # Check if done
179: if kill -0 $CLAUDE_PID 2>/dev/null; then
180:     echo "Still running..."
181: else
182:     echo "Done. Output in /tmp/tests-output.txt"
183: fi
184: 
185: # Wait for completion
186: wait $CLAUDE_PID
187: ```
188: 
189: ### Considerations
190: 
191: - Always use `--max-budget-usd` for background tasks to prevent runaway costs
192: - Redirect output to a file (`> /tmp/output.txt`) for later retrieval
193: - Use `$!` to capture the PID for status checking
194: - Background tasks compete for API rate limits
195: 
196: ---
197: 
198: ## 6. MODEL SELECTION STRATEGY
199: 
200: **Choose the right model tier for each delegated task.**
201: 
202: ### Decision Matrix
203: 
204: | Task Complexity | Model | Flag | Cost Tier |
205: |----------------|-------|------|-----------|
206: | Trivial (classify, format) | Haiku | `--model claude-haiku-5-5` | Low |
207: | Standard (review, generate) | Sonnet | `--model claude-sonnet-5-5` | Medium |
208: | Complex (architecture, debug) | Opus | `--model claude-opus-5-5 --effort high` | High |
209: 
210: ### Implementation
211: 
212: ```bash
213: # Tier 1: Haiku for fast, cheap tasks
214: claude -p "Classify these error messages by type: [errors]" \
215:   --model claude-haiku-5-5 --output-format text 2>&1
216: 
217: # Tier 2: Sonnet for standard tasks (default)
218: claude -p "Review @src/auth.ts for security issues" \
219:   --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
220: 
221: # Tier 3: Opus for complex reasoning
222: claude -p "Design the data migration strategy for moving from MongoDB to PostgreSQL" \
223:   --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort high --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
224: ```
225: 
226: ### Cost Optimization
227: 
228: ```bash
229: # Quick triage with Haiku, then deep dive with Opus on critical items
230: TRIAGE=$(claude -p "List the 3 most critical security issues in @src/auth/" \
231:   --model claude-haiku-5-5 --output-format text 2>&1)
232: 
233: DEEP_ANALYSIS=$(claude -p "Deep analysis of these security issues: $TRIAGE" \
234:   --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort high --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1)
235: ```
236: 
237: ---
238: 
239: ## 7. CONTEXT ENRICHMENT
240: 
241: **Provide rich context to Claude Code for better results.**
242: 
243: ### CLAUDE.md Context
244: 
245: Claude Code automatically loads CLAUDE.md files. Place project context there for consistent behavior:
246: 
247: ```
248: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md           → Global preferences
249: PROJECT_ROOT/CLAUDE.md        → Project conventions, architecture
250: SUBDIR/CLAUDE.md              → Module-specific context
251: ```
252: 
253: ### File References
254: 
255: Use `@` prefix to include file contents in prompts:
256: 
257: ```bash
258: # Single file
259: claude -p "Review @src/auth.ts" --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
260: 
261: # Multiple files
262: claude -p "Review @src/auth.ts and @src/middleware/auth.ts for consistency" \
263:   --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
264: 
265: # Combining context with task
266: claude -p "Given the patterns in @src/middleware/auth.ts, create similar middleware for rate limiting" \
267:   --output-format text 2>&1
268: ```
269: 
270: ### System Prompt Enhancement
271: 
272: ```bash
273: # Append context to system prompt
274: claude -p "Review this code" \
275:   --append-system-prompt "Project uses Express.js 4.x, TypeScript strict mode, and Jest for testing. Follow OWASP Top 10 guidelines." \
276:   --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
277: ```
278: 
279: ---
280: 
281: ## 8. VALIDATION PIPELINE
282: 
283: **Multi-stage validation using Claude Code at different levels.**
284: 
285: ### When to Use
286: 
287: - Pre-merge quality gates
288: - Complex feature development requiring multiple review dimensions
289: - Security-sensitive changes requiring independent validation
290: 
291: ### 5-Stage Pipeline
292: 
293: ```bash
294: # Stage 1: Syntax check (calling AI or local tools)
295: npx tsc --noEmit src/feature.ts
296: 
297: # Stage 2: Security review (Claude Code, read-only)
298: claude -p "Security audit of @src/feature.ts. Check OWASP Top 10." \
299:   --agent review --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1 > /tmp/security.md
300: 
301: # Stage 3: Architecture review (Claude Code, read-only)
302: claude -p "Does @src/feature.ts follow the patterns in @src/services/? Check coupling, error handling, typing." \
303:   --agent review --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1 > /tmp/arch.md
304: 
305: # Stage 4: Test coverage analysis (Claude Code, read-only)
306: claude -p "Analyze @src/feature.ts and suggest comprehensive test cases. Identify edge cases and error paths." \
307:   --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1 > /tmp/test-plan.md
308: 
309: # Stage 5: Final integration review (calling AI)
310: # Read all review outputs and make final decision
311: ```
312: 
313: ---
314: 
315: ## 9. CROSS-VALIDATION
316: 
317: **Use multiple AIs to validate the same artifact.**
318: 
319: ### When to Use
320: 
321: - High-stakes code changes (auth, payments, data handling)
322: - Architecture decisions that are hard to reverse
323: - Security audits where coverage matters more than speed
324: 
325: ### Implementation
326: 
327: ```bash
328: # Calling AI generates code, saves to /tmp/feature.ts
329: 
330: # Claude Code reviews
331: CLAUDE_REVIEW=$(claude -p "Review @/tmp/feature.ts for bugs and security issues" \
332:   --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1)
333: 
334: # OpenCode reviews (if available)
335: OPENCODE_REVIEW=$(opencode run "Review @/tmp/feature.ts for bugs and security issues" \
336:   --sandbox read-only --model gpt-5.3-opencode 2>&1)
337: 
338: # Calling AI synthesizes all reviews
339: # Compare findings, prioritize issues found by multiple AIs
340: ```
341: 
342: ### Considerations
343: 
344: - Cross-validation is expensive (3x cost) — reserve for critical code
345: - Focus on disagreements between AIs as areas needing human review
346: - Weight each AI's strengths: Claude for reasoning, OpenCode for sandbox safety and web context
347: 
348: ---
349: 
350: ## 10. SESSION CONTINUITY
351: 
352: **Continue conversations across invocations.**
353: 
354: ### When to Use
355: 
356: - Multi-step analysis where each step builds on the previous
357: - Iterative refinement of complex outputs
358: - Long-running investigations that span multiple invocations
359: 
360: ### Implementation
361: 
362: ```bash
363: # Initial analysis
364: claude -p "Analyze the auth module architecture" --output-format json 2>&1 > /tmp/session1.json
365: 
366: # Extract session info for resumption
367: SESSION_ID=$(jq -r '.session_id' /tmp/session1.json)
368: 
369: # Continue the conversation
370: claude -p "Now suggest improvements to the auth flow you identified" \
371:   --continue --output-format text 2>&1
372: 
373: # Or resume a specific session
374: claude -p "Apply the suggested improvements" \
375:   --resume "$SESSION_ID" --output-format text 2>&1
376: ```
377: 
378: ### Considerations
379: 
380: - `--continue` always continues the most recent session
381: - `--resume SESSION_ID` is more reliable for specific conversations
382: - Session context accumulates — watch for growing token usage and costs
383: - Use `--max-budget-usd` to cap cumulative session costs
384: 
385: ---
386: 
387: ## 11. ANTI-PATTERNS
388: 
389: ### Don't Do These
390: 
391: | Anti-Pattern | Problem | Better Approach |
392: |-------------|---------|-----------------|
393: | **Delegating trivial tasks** | CLI overhead > task cost | Handle simple tasks locally |
394: | **Skipping validation** | AI output can be wrong | Always validate before integrating |
395: | **Nesting Claude Code** | Undefined behavior when `$CLAUDECODE` is set | Check env var; use different terminal |
396: | **Ignoring costs** | Background tasks can accumulate | Always use `--max-budget-usd` |
397: | **Broad prompts** | "Review the whole project" overwhelms context | Target specific files with `@` |
398: | **Wrong model for task** | Opus for classification wastes money | Match model tier to complexity |
399: | **Skipping `2>&1`** | Lose error messages | Always capture stderr |
400: | **Trusting blindly** | Any AI can produce incorrect output | Cross-reference with codebase |
401: | **Rapid sequential calls** | Hit rate limits | Batch operations or add delays |
402: | **Using `bypassPermissions`** | Dangerous auto-approve | Always get explicit user approval |
403: 
404: ### Cost Awareness
405: 
406: ```
407: Approximate cost comparison (per 1K input + 1K output tokens):
408:   Haiku:  ~$0.001 (cheapest)
409:   Sonnet: ~$0.01  (10x haiku)
410:   Opus:   ~$0.05  (50x haiku)
411: 
412: Rule of thumb:
413:   - Haiku for batch/simple: $0.01-0.05 per task
414:   - Sonnet for standard: $0.05-0.25 per task
415:   - Opus for complex: $0.25-2.00 per task
416: 
417: Always use --max-budget-usd for batch operations.
418: ```

47: reader finds it. This section is the last in the file, and it holds the only pseudocode.
48:

51: 
52: SKILL_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
53: RESOURCE_BASES = (SKILL_ROOT / "references", SKILL_ROOT / "assets")
54:

57: 
58: INTENT_SIGNALS = {

60: }
61: 
62: RESOURCE_MAP = {
63:     "PRIMARY": ["{{DEFAULT_RESOURCE}}"],
64: }
65:

79:     docs = []
80:     for base in RESOURCE_BASES:
81:         if base.exists():

83:     return {doc.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix() for doc in docs}

86:     resolved = (SKILL_ROOT / relative_path).resolve()
87:     resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT)
88:     if resolved.suffix.lower() != ".md":
89:         raise ValueError(f"Only skill-local markdown resources are routable: {relative_path}")
90:     return resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix()

# CLI External Dispatch Hub (cli-external-orchestration)

One skill, three workflow modes, one shared `family: cli` identity. `cli-external-orchestration` is the public, advisor-routable home for every external CLI dispatch orchestrator in this repo. Before routing, the hub reads `hub-router.json` to resolve a `workflowMode`, then delegates through `mode-registry.json`. This hub holds NO per-mode logic — each mode keeps its own dispatch contract, self-invocation guard, and hard rules in its packet, and the hub only routes by `workflowMode`.

---

## 1. WHEN TO USE

Use this skill (through the hub) for any cross-AI CLI dispatch. Invoke it as `cli-external-orchestration`; the hub classifies the request, resolves a mode key, and loads the matching nested packet.

| Mode | Kind | Use it for | Packet |
|------|------|-----------|--------|
| **cli-opencode** | workflow | OpenCode CLI orchestration: external dispatch, in-OpenCode parallel/detached sessions, full plugin/skill/MCP/Spec-Kit-Memory runtime, small-model dispatch (DeepSeek, Kimi, MiniMax, MiMo, GLM) | `cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/` |
| **cli-claude-code** | workflow | Claude Code CLI orchestration: Anthropic-backed extended thinking, surgical code editing, structured JSON-schema output, agent delegation, cross-AI second opinions | `cli-external-orchestration/cli-claude-code/` |
| **cli-codex** | workflow | Codex CLI orchestration: OpenAI-backed coding, review, and web research; fails closed when `codex` is absent | `cli-external-orchestration/cli-codex/` |

### When NOT to Use

- The current runtime IS the target CLI — each mode's own self-invocation guard refuses self-dispatch (see that packet's §2); this hub does no dispatch itself and carries no guard of its own.
- Application-code implementation, review, or design work with no CLI-dispatch need — use `sk-code` / `sk-design` directly.
- A quick in-process task with no cross-AI handoff — dispatching to an external CLI process is unnecessary overhead.

---

## 2. SMART ROUTING

Routing is registry-driven. `mode-registry.json` lists all three modes in one `modes[]` array. `hub-router.json` decides whether the result is a single mode, an ordered bundle, or a deferred disambiguation.

> **Compiled routing (default-on, flag-gated, additive).** Resolve the mode via the compiled router contract first:
> ```bash
> node .opencode/bin/compiled-route.cjs --hub cli-external-orchestration --prompt "<task>"
> ```
> Follow the returned decision — `route` (use its `targets`), `clarify`/`defer` (disambiguate), `reject` (refuse). On a `{"servingAuthority":"legacy"}` sentinel or any error, use the routing below. The front door self-gates on serving-authority. Compiled routing is now the default for `cli-external-orchestration`; set `SPECKIT_COMPILED_ROUTING=0` to force legacy routing fleet-wide — the explicit kill-switch.

### Two-Axis Model

- `packetKind: "workflow"` — `cli-opencode`, `cli-claude-code`, and `cli-codex` orchestrate a CLI binary and their dispatched writes land in THIS repo's workspace (`mutatesWorkspace:true`). None is a transport packet: all classify intent, choose/confirm a provider, and conduct the dispatched session.
- Zero extensions: no surface-axis, no transport-axis, no runtime-loop. All three modes are primary, independently-routable dispatch workflows.

### Routing Rule

```text
read hub-router.json
  -> score routerSignals and vocabularyClasses
  -> apply routerPolicy.tieBreak
  -> read mode-registry.json for packetKind, backendKind, toolSurface, and advisorRouting
  -> load the selected packet(s)
```

### Outcomes

- `single`: one dominant executor signal routes to one mode.
- `orderedBundle`: multiple explicitly requested executors route in tie-break order.
- `defer`: unclear or contradictory dispatch intent asks for disambiguation — the router does not silently default to `cli-opencode` on genuine ambiguity.

### Executor Delegation

A prompt naming a specific executor (e.g. "use cli-opencode", "delegate to opencode", "get a claude code second opinion", "delegate to codex", or a small model that dispatches through one) is resolved by the system-skill-advisor's executor-delegation scorer, which sources its alias table from THIS hub's `mode-registry.json` — keyed by each mode's `packetSkillName` — and resolves to `cli-opencode`, `cli-claude-code`, or `cli-codex`. See `system-skill-advisor/mcp-server/lib/scorer/executor-delegation.ts`.

## 4. RULES

### ✅ ALWAYS

- Resolve packets through `mode-registry.json`; never hardcode packet roots in prose-only logic.
- Keep `SKILL.md` thin: routing, invariants, and navigation only.
- Keep every packet in `modes[]` and give every packet a `packetKind`.
- Keep exactly one `graph-metadata.json`, at the hub root.
- Keep `hub-router.json` signal keys and registry `workflowMode` values bidirectionally aligned.
- Read the target mode's `SKILL.md` before composing any dispatch prompt (constitutional cli-dispatch-skill-preload rule) — the advisor recommendation alone does not waive this.

### ⛔ NEVER

- Never add a second packet array.
- Never add packet-local `graph-metadata.json` files.
- Never let any mode dispatch itself — the self-invocation guard is packet-owned and non-negotiable.
- Never let the executor CLI (the HOW) override the calling skill's own workflow (the WHAT) — "use cli-opencode gpt-5.5 high" still runs inside the caller's skill-owned route.

### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF

- A packet cannot be classified as `workflow` (all three current modes are; a future mode may not be).
- Router signals, vocabulary classes, and registry modes cannot be made bidirectionally consistent.
- The executor-delegation scorer resolves a delegation prompt to `cli-external-orchestration` itself instead of a real executor — that is the exact silent-misroute failure mode ADR-005 rewrote the scorer to prevent; report it rather than working around it.

# CLI External Dispatch Hub (cli-external-orchestration)

One skill, three workflow modes, one shared `family: cli` identity. `cli-external-orchestration` is the public, advisor-routable home for every external CLI dispatch orchestrator in this repo. Before routing, the hub reads `hub-router.json` to resolve a `workflowMode`, then delegates through `mode-registry.json`. This hub holds NO per-mode logic — each mode keeps its own dispatch contract, self-invocation guard, and hard rules in its packet, and the hub only routes by `workflowMode`.

---

## 1. WHEN TO USE

Use this skill (through the hub) for any cross-AI CLI dispatch. Invoke it as `cli-external-orchestration`; the hub classifies the request, resolves a mode key, and loads the matching nested packet.

| Mode | Kind | Use it for | Packet |
|------|------|-----------|--------|
| **cli-opencode** | workflow | OpenCode CLI orchestration: external dispatch, in-OpenCode parallel/detached sessions, full plugin/skill/MCP/Spec-Kit-Memory runtime, small-model dispatch (DeepSeek, Kimi, MiniMax, MiMo, GLM) | `cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/` |
| **cli-claude-code** | workflow | Claude Code CLI orchestration: Anthropic-backed extended thinking, surgical code editing, structured JSON-schema output, agent delegation, cross-AI second opinions | `cli-external-orchestration/cli-claude-code/` |
| **cli-codex** | workflow | Codex CLI orchestration: OpenAI-backed coding, review, and web research; fails closed when `codex` is absent | `cli-external-orchestration/cli-codex/` |

### When NOT to Use

- The current runtime IS the target CLI — each mode's own self-invocation guard refuses self-dispatch (see that packet's §2); this hub does no dispatch itself and carries no guard of its own.
- Application-code implementation, review, or design work with no CLI-dispatch need — use `sk-code` / `sk-design` directly.
- A quick in-process task with no cross-AI handoff — dispatching to an external CLI process is unnecessary overhead.

---

## 2. SMART ROUTING

Routing is registry-driven. `mode-registry.json` lists all three modes in one `modes[]` array. `hub-router.json` decides whether the result is a single mode, an ordered bundle, or a deferred disambiguation.

> **Compiled routing (default-on, flag-gated, additive).** Resolve the mode via the compiled router contract first:
> ```bash
> node .opencode/bin/compiled-route.cjs --hub cli-external-orchestration --prompt "<task>"
> ```
> Follow the returned decision — `route` (use its `targets`), `clarify`/`defer` (disambiguate), `reject` (refuse). On a `{"servingAuthority":"legacy"}` sentinel or any error, use the routing below. The front door self-gates on serving-authority. Compiled routing is now the default for `cli-external-orchestration`; set `SPECKIT_COMPILED_ROUTING=0` to force legacy routing fleet-wide — the explicit kill-switch.

### Two-Axis Model

- `packetKind: "workflow"` — `cli-opencode`, `cli-claude-code`, and `cli-codex` orchestrate a CLI binary and their dispatched writes land in THIS repo's workspace (`mutatesWorkspace:true`). None is a transport packet: all classify intent, choose/confirm a provider, and conduct the dispatched session.
- Zero extensions: no surface-axis, no transport-axis, no runtime-loop. All three modes are primary, independently-routable dispatch workflows.

### Routing Rule

```text
read hub-router.json
  -> score routerSignals and vocabularyClasses
  -> apply routerPolicy.tieBreak
  -> read mode-registry.json for packetKind, backendKind, toolSurface, and advisorRouting
  -> load the selected packet(s)
```

### Outcomes

- `single`: one dominant executor signal routes to one mode.
- `orderedBundle`: multiple explicitly requested executors route in tie-break order.
- `defer`: unclear or contradictory dispatch intent asks for disambiguation — the router does not silently default to `cli-opencode` on genuine ambiguity.

### Executor Delegation

A prompt naming a specific executor (e.g. "use cli-opencode", "delegate to opencode", "get a claude code second opinion", "delegate to codex", or a small model that dispatches through one) is resolved by the system-skill-advisor's executor-delegation scorer, which sources its alias table from THIS hub's `mode-registry.json` — keyed by each mode's `packetSkillName` — and resolves to `cli-opencode`, `cli-claude-code`, or `cli-codex`. See `system-skill-advisor/mcp-server/lib/scorer/executor-delegation.ts`.

### Companion Metadata

- `mode-registry.json` owns `workflowMode`, `packetKind`, `backendKind`, `toolSurface`, packet folder identity, alias phrases, and `advisorRouting`. It is also the executor-delegation scorer's source of truth for which CLI executors exist.
- `hub-router.json` owns `routerPolicy`, `routerSignals`, `vocabularyClasses`.
- `description.json` owns advisor-facing summary fields.
- `graph-metadata.json` owns the one skill-graph identity node for the whole hub (`family: cli`).

### Self-Invocation Guards Stay Packet-Local

Each mode's self-invocation guard is runtime-signal-based (env var / process ancestry / lockfile), not path-based, so it is unaffected by this hub's routing layer. `cli-opencode` additionally carries a parallel-detached carve-out that `cli-claude-code` intentionally does not — that asymmetry is preserved.

---

## 4. RULES

### ✅ ALWAYS

- Resolve packets through `mode-registry.json`; never hardcode packet roots in prose-only logic.
- Keep `SKILL.md` thin: routing, invariants, and navigation only.
- Keep every packet in `modes[]` and give every packet a `packetKind`.
- Keep exactly one `graph-metadata.json`, at the hub root.
- Keep `hub-router.json` signal keys and registry `workflowMode` values bidirectionally aligned.
- Read the target mode's `SKILL.md` before composing any dispatch prompt (constitutional cli-dispatch-skill-preload rule) — the advisor recommendation alone does not waive this.

### ⛔ NEVER

- Never add a second packet array.
- Never add packet-local `graph-metadata.json` files.
- Never let any mode dispatch itself — the self-invocation guard is packet-owned and non-negotiable.
- Never let the executor CLI (the HOW) override the calling skill's own workflow (the WHAT) — "use cli-opencode gpt-5.5 high" still runs inside the caller's skill-owned route.

### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF

- A packet cannot be classified as `workflow` (all three current modes are; a future mode may not be).
- Router signals, vocabulary classes, and registry modes cannot be made bidirectionally consistent.
- The executor-delegation scorer resolves a delegation prompt to `cli-external-orchestration` itself instead of a real executor — that is the exact silent-misroute failure mode ADR-005 rewrote the scorer to prevent; report it rather than working around it.

31: ## 2. INTENT MODEL
32: 
33: - **DEEP_REASONING** — "reason / think / analyze / trade-off / architecture / extended thinking / root cause / pros and cons / step by step / weigh the options" requests load `references/cli-reference.md` and `references/claude-tools.md`, the flags an Opus reasoning dispatch needs plus the capability comparison that justifies it.

35: - **STRUCTURED_OUTPUT** — "json / schema / structured / extract / validate output / --json-schema / machine-readable / guaranteed structure" requests load `references/cli-reference.md` and `references/claude-tools.md`, for the `--json-schema` flag and the only capability that makes the delegation worth it.
36: - **REVIEW** — "review / audit / security / quality / second opinion / cross-validate / pre-merge / double-check" requests load `references/integration-patterns.md` and `references/agent-delegation.md`, the cross-AI review pattern plus the `review` agent that runs it read-only.

51: ### Prerequisite Detection
52: 
53: ```bash
54: # Verify Claude Code CLI is available before routing
55: command -v claude || echo "Not installed. Run: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code"
56: 
57: # SELF-INVOCATION GUARD: inside Claude Code, never shell out to claude. Dispatch a native subagent (Agent tool); it inherits the session's effort, and an agent definition's `effort` field sets a different one.
58: [ -n "$CLAUDECODE" ] && echo "ERROR: Already inside Claude Code session. Do not self-invoke."
59: ```
60: 
61: ### Self-Invocation Guard
62: 
63: ```python
64: def detect_self_invocation():
65:     """Returns a non-None signal when the orchestrator is already running inside Claude Code."""
66:     # Layer 1: env var lookup — Claude Code sets CLAUDECODE on session start
67:     if os.environ.get('CLAUDECODE'):
68:         return ('env', 'CLAUDECODE')
69:     # Layer 2: process ancestry — claude in parent tree
70:     try:
71:         ancestry = subprocess.check_output(['ps', '-o', 'command=', '-p', str(os.getppid())]).decode()
72:         if '/claude' in ancestry or 'claude ' in ancestry:
73:             return ('ancestry', 'claude')
74:     except subprocess.SubprocessError:
75:         pass
76:     # Layer 3: state lock-file probe
77:     state_dir = os.path.expanduser('~/.claude/state')
78:     if os.path.isdir(state_dir):
79:         for entry in os.listdir(state_dir):
80:             if os.path.exists(os.path.join(state_dir, entry, 'lock')):
81:                 return ('lockfile', entry)
82:     return None
83: 
84: if detect_self_invocation():

87:         "Use a sibling cli-* skill or a fresh shell session in a different runtime to dispatch a different model."

A session already running inside Claude Code never reaches this router, because the self-invocation guard refuses it first.
24: 
25: The router answers one question: given a request, which skill-local resources load, in what order, and
26: what happens when nothing matches. Every path below stays inside this skill folder, and no resource
27: loads before an intent selects it.
28: 
29: ---
30: 
31: ## 2. INTENT MODEL
32: 
33: - **DEEP_REASONING** — "reason / think / analyze / trade-off / architecture / extended thinking / root cause / pros and cons / step by step / weigh the options" requests load `references/cli-reference.md` and `references/claude-tools.md`, the flags an Opus reasoning dispatch needs plus the capability comparison that justifies it.
34: - **CODE_EDITING** — "edit / refactor / modify / fix / surgical edit / diff-based / rewrite / multi-file edit / preserve existing patterns" requests load `references/cli-reference.md` and `assets/prompt-templates.md`, the invocation flags before the prompt shaped for a diff-based edit.
35: - **STRUCTURED_OUTPUT** — "json / schema / structured / extract / validate output / --json-schema / machine-readable / guaranteed structure" requests load `references/cli-reference.md` and `references/claude-tools.md`, for the `--json-schema` flag and the only capability that makes the delegation worth it.
36: - **REVIEW** — "review / audit / security / quality / second opinion / cross-validate / pre-merge / double-check" requests load `references/integration-patterns.md` and `references/agent-delegation.md`, the cross-AI review pattern plus the `review` agent that runs it read-only.
37: - **AGENT_DELEGATION** — "delegate / agent / background / parallel / offload / plan mode / read-only exploration / hand off" requests load `references/agent-delegation.md` and `references/integration-patterns.md`, the roster that picks the agent and the pattern that hands the work over.
38: - **TEMPLATES** — "template / prompt / how to ask / how do I phrase / wording / boilerplate" requests load `assets/prompt-templates.md` and `references/cli-reference.md`, a ready-made prompt before the flags it is paired with.
39: - **PATTERNS** — "pattern / workflow / orchestrate / session / continue / resume / cross-ai / pick up where we left off" requests load `references/integration-patterns.md` and `references/cli-reference.md`, where session continuity and orchestration meet.
40: - **DESIGN** — "sk-design-md-generator / extract design system / generate design.md / style reference / design tokens / css extraction" requests load no file here on purpose: the intent is a handoff, so it routes the work out to `sk-design-md-generator` and `RESOURCE_MAP` keeps no DESIGN entry.

44: ## 3. MACHINE ROUTER
45: 
46: The one machine-readable projection of the intent model above, written as `## MACHINE ROUTER` so every

49: This section holds the packet's prerequisite probe, self-invocation guard, loading levels, intent dictionaries and call sequence.

51: ### Prerequisite Detection
52: 
53: ```bash
54: # Verify Claude Code CLI is available before routing
55: command -v claude || echo "Not installed. Run: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code"
56: 
57: # SELF-INVOCATION GUARD: inside Claude Code, never shell out to claude. Dispatch a native subagent (Agent tool); it inherits the session's effort, and an agent definition's `effort` field sets a different one.
58: [ -n "$CLAUDECODE" ] && echo "ERROR: Already inside Claude Code session. Do not self-invoke."
59: ```
60: 
61: ### Self-Invocation Guard
62: 
63: ```python
64: def detect_self_invocation():
65:     """Returns a non-None signal when the orchestrator is already running inside Claude Code."""
66:     # Layer 1: env var lookup — Claude Code sets CLAUDECODE on session start
67:     if os.environ.get('CLAUDECODE'):
68:         return ('env', 'CLAUDECODE')
69:     # Layer 2: process ancestry — claude in parent tree
70:     try:
71:         ancestry = subprocess.check_output(['ps', '-o', 'command=', '-p', str(os.getppid())]).decode()
72:         if '/claude' in ancestry or 'claude ' in ancestry:
73:             return ('ancestry', 'claude')
74:     except subprocess.SubprocessError:
75:         pass
76:     # Layer 3: state lock-file probe
77:     state_dir = os.path.expanduser('~/.claude/state')
78:     if os.path.isdir(state_dir):
79:         for entry in os.listdir(state_dir):
80:             if os.path.exists(os.path.join(state_dir, entry, 'lock')):
81:                 return ('lockfile', entry)
82:     return None
83: 
84: if detect_self_invocation():
85:     refuse(
86:         "Self-invocation refused: this agent is already running inside Claude Code. "
87:         "Use a sibling cli-* skill or a fresh shell session in a different runtime to dispatch a different model."
88:     )
89: ```
